title: Muharram: the month of Allah
hook: the best fasting after Ramadan is in Muharram (Muslim)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the sacred months: three in a row, Rajab alone, and a verse that says, wrong not yourselves in them. Today, one of the four, up close.

After Ramadan, which fast is best? In Sahih Muslim, that question is put to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and Abu Hurayrah reports his answer. It doesn't name a single day. It names a whole month, and gives that month a title you won't find printed on a calendar page. Not the month of the new year. Not the month of fasting. The month of Allah.
screen: `AFTER RAMADAN, WHICH FAST?` → `A WHOLE MONTH.` → `THE MONTH OF ALLAH.`

segments.voice: Here is the hadith, in paraphrase: the best fasting after Ramadan is in Allah's month, al-Muharram, and the best prayer after the obligatory prayers is the prayer at night. One sentence, two offerings: an empty stomach by day, a person standing awake at night. Then the name. Every month belongs to Allah, Muslims say, so why call this one Allah's month? Some scholars explain it the way they explain the phrase house of Allah for a mosque. Every place is His, but naming one place after Him lifts it and sets it apart. And Muharram is already one of the four sacred months, the third of the three in a row. You met it back in year two as the start of the Islamic year, as tradition counts it. Now the part that's easy to miss: none of this is required. Ramadan's fast is a duty. Muharram's is an offer. The word in the hadith is best, not must. Nobody is told to fast the whole month. A person can take one day, or a few, and they're stepping into what the hadith praises. So Muharram is an open door at the start of the year. And it gives the fast a life outside Ramadan. A practice that only happens once a year can start to feel like a costume. A voluntary day in Muharram says the fast belongs to ordinary time too.
screen: `A FAST BY DAY, A PRAYER BY NIGHT.` · `WHY CALL IT ALLAH'S MONTH?` · `AN OFFER, NOT A DUTY.` · `THE FAST IN ORDINARY TIME.`

segments.voice: If you fast, pick one day this Muharram, or the next time it comes, and see it on the calendar in your mind; if you don't, choose something small to hold back from for one day, a snack, a scroll, a second coffee. Notice what it's like to choose an offering nobody requires of you. If you pray, you can remember the night prayer the same hadith praises.
Muharram. A sacred month, called Allah's month in Sahih Muslim, where voluntary fasting is praised as the best after Ramadan. Today's word.
Your line: allah's month. An offer, not a duty. That's day one thousand three hundred fifty-four.

chat.says: Do Muslims have to fast in Muharram the way they do in Ramadan?
options: No. It's an offer, not a duty; the hadith calls fasting in it the best after Ramadan.
Yes. Muharram's fast is a duty, required for the whole month like Ramadan.
No. Fasting in Muharram is discouraged, since it's the month of the new year.
chat.meaning: In Sahih Muslim, the best fasting after Ramadan is in Allah's month, al-Muharram. The word is best, not must: a voluntary offer.
